problem: The population of pines in a forest increases by $100$ trees every year. What differential equation describes the rate of change of the population $P(t)$ of the pines? Assume that the time $t$ is measured in years.

feedback.worked_solution:
If the volume of water remaining is $V,$ then the rate of change of the volume is $\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t},$ where $t$ is the time in hours.

Since $14$ cubic meters of water are released each hour, the rate of change of the volume is given by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=-14.
$$

The right-hand side is negative because the volume of water is *decreasing*.
